extracted.intended_audience: fiction writers, readers, and community moderators interested in distinguishing literary and genre fiction
extracted.subtask_description: Identify whether a work aligns more with 'literary' or a particular 'genre' by applying distinguishing hallmarks, evaluation standards, and community expectation guidance. Useful for writers deciding tone/market and for readers/moderators evaluating stories against community norms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of literary fiction
rubrics_metrics.description: "Fiction that cannot be categorized by any specific genre conventions, and which seeks to describe real-life reactions to complex events using well-developed characters, themes, literary devices, and experimentations in prose."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this as the working definition: emphasis on complex characters, thematic inquiry into the human condition, formal or stylistic experimentation. Not defined by plot-driven genre conventions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Character over plot
rubrics_metrics.description: Interior focus, psychological complexity, and character development are prioritized over forward-moving plot.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate scenes for interiority and character nuance rather than plot mechanics; look for explorations of motive, perception, and change. This is a hallmark of literary fiction and often contrasts with genre expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stylistic ambition
rubrics_metrics.description: Sentence-level craft is foregrounded; style and voice are deliberate artistic concerns.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess diction, syntactic variety, and formal experimentation. Stylistic risks and distinctive prose can be primary goals rather than mere vehicles for plot.

rubrics_metrics.name: Thematic depth
rubrics_metrics.description: Engages 'the human condition' and pursues complexity, ambiguity, and layered themes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Look for sustained thematic inquiry, philosophical or social resonance, and work that raises questions rather than just resolving them. Depth is measured by nuance and multiplicity of meaning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of literary devices
rubrics_metrics.description: Employs metaphor, symbolism, allegory, defamiliarization, and other devices as central tools.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate how devices contribute to theme and interiority rather than solely ornamenting plot. Consider whether symbolism and allegory open interpretive possibilities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Possibly non-conventional structure
rubrics_metrics.description: May use fragmented timelines, multiple perspectives, or other experimental structures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Structural experimentation can be a deliberate feature—assess coherence, purposefulness, and how structure serves character and theme rather than expecting linear plot progression.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ambiguous or unsatisfying endings acceptable
rubrics_metrics.description: No guarantee of a 'satisfying' or closed ending; ambiguity is often valued.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not penalize lack of closure when assessing literary work; ambiguity may be an artistic choice aligning with thematic aims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prose foregrounded
rubrics_metrics.description: Language itself is a focus; prose may be foregrounded over plot mechanics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess sentencecraft and linguistic choices as central to the work's value; stylistic moves may be the primary site of meaning-making.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of genre fiction
rubrics_metrics.description: Stories that operate within conventions of a recognized category (sci‑fi, fantasy, mystery, romance, thriller, horror, YA, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify the relevant genre's conventions and measure the work against those expectations: plot momentum, trope usage, and reader satisfaction are central.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plot over interiority (genre tendency)
rubrics_metrics.description: Genre fiction often prioritizes plot, external stakes, and narrative momentum over interior psychological exploration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate pacing, causal plotting, and the clarity of narrative propulsion. In many genres, maintaining momentum is a key quality metric.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conventions honored
rubrics_metrics.description: Readers buy genre expecting certain conventions; honoring those conventions is often a quality criterion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Determine which conventions the target audience expects (e.g., detective solves case, romance ends in HEA) and whether the work satisfies, subverts, or reinvents them purposefully.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pacing prioritized
rubrics_metrics.description: Story momentum and pacing are important quality markers in genre fiction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess scene beats, tension arcs, and whether the narrative maintains engagement appropriate to the genre (faster pacing in thrillers, measured reveal in mysteries, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Resolution expected
rubrics_metrics.description: Closed endings are standard in many genres (happy-ever-after in romance, solved case in mystery).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judge whether the ending meets the genre's closure expectations; failure to resolve core genre questions may be perceived as dissatisfaction by readers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Worldbuilding (genre feature)
rubrics_metrics.description: Extensive worldbuilding is often a hallmark of fantasy and science fiction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate the plausibility, internal consistency, and relevance of the worldbuilding to plot and character. Good worldbuilding enhances stakes and reader immersion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Genre-specific tropes
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of known tropes appropriate to the genre; these may be deployed or subverted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess how tropes are used—whether they fulfill reader expectations, are innovatively subverted, or feel clichéd. Successful tropes often serve plot and character effectively.

rubrics_metrics.name: Spectrum / hybrid positions
rubrics_metrics.description: Works fall on a spectrum from pure literary to pulp/commercial genre; many authors blend elements (e.g., literary with genre elements, high-craft genre).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid binary labeling. Use spectrum placement to explain how works prioritize different axes (voice, plot, theme, convention). Examples given: Toni Morrison (pure literary); Kazuo Ishiguro (literary with sci‑fi elements); Ursula Le Guin (high‑craft genre); Stephen King (mid‑genre).

rubrics_metrics.name: Literary evaluation criteria (quality standards)
rubrics_metrics.description: Literary works are judged on prose, theme, originality, depth, and complexity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When evaluating a literary work, foreground craft of language, thematic ambition, originality of perspective, and complexity of character and structure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Genre evaluation criteria (quality standards)
rubrics_metrics.description: Genre works are judged on convention-execution, pace, satisfaction, world-building, and tropes deployed/subverted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When evaluating genre fiction, prioritize how well the work meets genre-specific expectations: pacing, satisfying resolution (as appropriate), believable worldbuilding, and effective use/subversion of tropes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Match audience/community expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: Reader communities judge by genre expectations; mismatches lead to penalization (e.g., literary story in a genre-friendly community gets penalized).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider the intended audience or community norms before posting. A work judged outside its expected criteria may be perceived as 'shallow' or 'unsatisfying' depending on the evaluative frame.

rubrics_metrics.name: Literary-as-genre conventions (Mythcreants critique)
rubrics_metrics.description: Argument that 'literary fiction' itself functions as a genre with conventions: MFA‑trained voice, quiet domestic drama, open endings, workshop-epiphany structure, privileged class settings, anti‑plot bias.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this perspective to recognize that 'literary' has recognizable, repeatable conventions; beware of assuming 'literary' equals objectively superior—it's another set of expectations that can be gamed or stereotyped.
